meta.title: Case Zero
meta.description: A prominent financier is found dead in his locked study. As the city's last honest detective, you have four locations to investigate. Gather evidence, link the pieces on your board, and name the killer before they vanish.

rooms.name: Detective's Office
rooms.description: Your cluttered office. Rain hammers the window. A corkboard on the wall holds everything you have so far. The phone rings twice then stops. Time to work.

rooms.name: Harbour Docks
rooms.description: Salt-stiff ropes and the smell of diesel. Shipping crates stacked to the sky. The harbormaster's shack sits at the far end of the pier, padlocked but accessible with the right persuasion.

rooms.name: Riverside Manor
rooms.description: The victim's grand home, now a crime scene. Yellow tape across the front door, but the side gate is open. Inside: an overturned desk, a smashed decanter, and the faint scent of expensive cologne.

rooms.name: The Noir Café
rooms.description: A cramped corner café that never closes. Jazz bleeds through the walls. Everyone in this city has sat in one of these booths at some point — including the people you're looking for.

items.name: Case File
items.description: The initial police report. Victim: Victor Hale, financier. Cause of death: blunt force trauma. Time of death: between 10 PM and midnight.
items.examineText: Victor Hale was found dead in his locked study at midnight by his housekeeper. No signs of forced entry. Three people had keys: his business partner Nadia Voss, his estranged nephew Roland Hale, and the household manager Mr. Ash.

items.name: Shipping Manifest
items.description: A dock manifest with certain line items circled in red ink.
items.examineText: Several large crates marked 'glassware' were loaded onto a vessel registered to Voss & Hale Imports on the night of the murder. The loading time logged is 11:30 PM — but the crates are not in the import registry.

items.name: Broken Pocket Watch
items.description: A gold pocket watch, stopped at 10:47 PM, found wedged between dock planks.
items.examineText: The initials 'R.H.' are engraved on the case. Roland Hale's watch — here, at the docks, at 10:47 PM. The night of the murder.

items.name: Monogrammed Cufflink
items.description: A single silver cufflink engraved with the letter V, found near the study window.
items.examineText: The monogram matches Nadia Voss's personal stationary style. It was found on the study floor — placing her inside the room on the night of the murder.

items.name: Threatening Letter
items.description: An unsigned letter found in the victim's desk. The handwriting is deliberate and angry.
items.examineText: The letter reads: 'You cannot keep taking what is not yours. Return what belongs to the family or I will take it back myself.' Forensics confirmed the paper stock is the same batch as a notepad found in Roland Hale's flat.

items.name: Torn Ledger Page
items.description: A single page torn from a financial ledger, hidden beneath a loose floorboard.
items.examineText: The page documents a secret account under a false name, funnelling money from Hale's estate to an offshore account. The account access codes are written in Nadia Voss's handwriting.

items.name: Café Matchbook
items.description: A matchbook from this very café, with a time and table number scrawled inside: '10 PM, table 4'.
items.examineText: A barista confirms two people met at table 4 at 10 PM on the night of the murder: a tall woman in a grey coat matching Nadia Voss's description, and an older man matching Mr. Ash. They argued in hushed voices for thirty minutes then left separately.

items.name: Dock Testimony
items.description: Written statement from the night-shift dock worker.
items.examineText: The dock worker recalls seeing a man matching Roland Hale's description loading the unregistered crates personally, then making a call from the pier payphone before leaving in a hurry around 11 PM.

items.name: Witness Statement
items.description: A sworn statement from the café's regular patron.
items.examineText: The patron overheard Nadia Voss tell Mr. Ash: 'Tonight is the only night. After this no one can prove anything.' This was at approximately 10:25 PM on the night of the murder.

deductions.text: Nadia Voss was inside the study on the night of the murder.
deductions.message: The cufflink places Voss at the scene.

deductions.text: Nadia Voss was embezzling from Hale and needed to silence him.
deductions.message: The ledger and manifest reveal a clear financial motive.

deductions.text: Voss coordinated the murder plan with Ash the same night it happened.
deductions.message: The café meeting and overheard conversation confirm premeditation.

deductions.text: Roland Hale was at the docks during the time of the murder — not at the manor.
deductions.message: Roland's watch and the dock worker's testimony place him elsewhere.

deductions.text: Roland Hale had a grievance against the victim and had threatened him.
deductions.message: The letter shows Roland's anger, but his alibi holds.

hints.text: Ask the dock workers about unusual activity on the night in question. The shipping manifest is a good starting point for the conversation.
The study has three areas to investigate: the desk, the floor near the window, and the loose floorboard under the rug.
Order something — the barista talks more freely if you're a paying customer. Ask about the night of the murder.

events.name: Question the Dock Workers
events.description: The night-shift workers know more than they're letting on. Work through the right questions.

steps.description: Show the shipping manifest to the dock foreman and ask about the unregistered crates.

action.label: Show Manifest to Foreman
action.failMessage: You need the shipping manifest before confronting the foreman.

effects.name: foreman-questioned
effects.message: The foreman shifts uncomfortably and admits the crates were loaded by someone who claimed to be Hale's nephew.

steps.description: Press for a written statement from the night-shift dock worker.

effects.message: The dock worker signs a statement confirming the man's identity and the timeline.

onComplete.name: docks-investigated
onComplete.message: You have everything the docks can offer.

events.name: Search the Study
events.description: The victim's study is a crime scene, but the police missed things. Work through it systematically.

steps.description: Examine the overturned desk for anything the police overlooked.

effects.name: desk-searched
effects.message: Under a scattered pile of papers you find a threatening letter. The handwriting is deliberate — almost practised.

steps.description: Check the floor near the window where the struggle apparently occurred.

effects.name: window-searched
effects.message: Something glints near the skirting board — a silver cufflink.

steps.description: Lift the rug and check the loose floorboard you noticed earlier.

effects.message: Concealed under the floorboard: a single torn ledger page. Someone hid this in a hurry.

onComplete.name: manor-investigated
onComplete.message: The study has given up its secrets.

events.name: Interview the Witness
events.description: A regular at the café claims to have seen something important on the night of the murder.

steps.description: Order coffee and strike up conversation with the barista.

effects.name: barista-chatted
effects.message: The barista mentions that one of the regulars was here the same night and might have seen something.

steps.description: Find the regular patron and ask what they witnessed that night.

effects.message: The patron provides a written account of the hushed argument they overheard.

onComplete.name: cafe-investigated
onComplete.message: The café has told you what it knows.

suspects.name: Nadia Voss
suspects.notReadyMessage: You need stronger evidence before accusing Nadia Voss. Keep investigating.
suspects.accuseMessage: You lay out your case against Nadia Voss: access, motive, and a premeditated plan coordinated with her accomplice.

suspects.name: Roland Hale
suspects.accuseMessage: You accuse Roland Hale based on the threatening letter and his presence at the docks.

suspects.name: Mr. Ash
suspects.accuseMessage: You accuse Mr. Ash based on his clandestine meeting with Voss on the night of the murder.

endings.title: Case Closed
endings.text: Nadia Voss's composure cracks when you present the evidence. The cufflink, the ledger, the café meeting — it's airtight. She embezzled for years and when Hale found out she arranged for his silence permanently. Mr. Ash, her unwilling accomplice, corroborates everything to shorten his own sentence. Justice is slow in this city. Tonight, it moves.

endings.title: Wrong Call
endings.text: Your accusation crumbles under cross-examination. The suspect's alibi holds. The real perpetrator has had time to disappear — along with any remaining evidence. The case goes cold. The city keeps its secrets. You sit in your empty office and wonder what you missed.
